docs.title: 🛡️ OWASP Juice Shop Application Security Portfolio
docs.text: A deep-dive, industry-grade security audit and white-box vulnerability assessment of the OWASP Juice Shop application, covering 100+ challenges across all 6 difficulty tiers.

docs.title: 📌 Executive Overview
docs.text:
This repository and documentation suite serves as an Application Security (AppSec) Engineering & Web Penetration Testing Portfolio. Rather than simply documenting exploit payloads or CTF flags, this project demonstrates an end-to-end security engineering approach:

flowchart LR
    Recon["🔍 1. Reconnaissance
& Attack Surface Mapping"] --> Exploit["💥 2. Ethical Proof-of-Concept
& CVSS v3.1 Scoring"]
    Exploit --> RootCause["🔬 3. White-Box Code Audit
(Node.js / Express / Angular)"]
    RootCause --> Remediation["🛡️ 4. Secure Coding Patches
& Defense-in-Depth"]

Each write-up adheres to enterprise vulnerability reporting standards, connecting business risk with technical root causes and developer remediation guides.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose of this Portfolio
docs.text:
This project was built to document an exhaustive, white-box security review of the OWASP Juice Shop vulnerable web application.

Key objectives demonstrated in this repository: 1. Systematic Vulnerability Assessment: Applying standard penetration testing methodologies (OWASP WSTG) from reconnaissance to exploitation. 2. Technical Depth: Going beyond standard CTF flags to locate flawed code statements inside the application codebase and explain why the vulnerability exists. 3. Actionable Remediasi: Formulating defensive patches and secure coding patterns directly usable by software engineering teams. 4. Professional Documentation: Producing clear, reproducible, and executive-ready vulnerability reports.

docs.text: [!NOTE] All testing was conducted ethically in a controlled local laboratory environment for educational and defense-readiness purposes.

docs.title: 3.1 Step-by-Step Reproduction
docs.text:
1. Navigate to http://<target-ip>:3000/#/<endpoint>.
  2. Intercept the request via Burp Suite Proxy.
  3. Observe the vulnerable parameter: 
    POST /api/vulnerable-endpoint HTTP/1.1
Host: target:3000
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "param": "payload_here"
}
  4. Send the crafted payload and observe the response: 
    HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "status": "success",
  "data": [...]
}

docs.text:
Attach screenshots showing Burp Suite request/response, browser behavior, or challenge solve notification.

docs.title: 4.1 Vulnerable Source Code
docs.text:
• Repository File: routes/<vulnerable-file>.ts (or frontend/src/...)
  • Vulnerable Lines: Lines XX - YY
// VULNERABLE CODE PATTERN
models.sequelize.query(`SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email}' AND password = '${security.hash(req.body.password)}'`)
  .then(([user]) => {
    // Unsafe handling
  });

docs.title: 4.2 Root Cause Breakdown
docs.text: Explain why the code failed: - Mechanism: Direct string concatenation of untrusted client input (req.body.email) into the database query without parameterized binding or input sanitization. - Architectural Flaw: Lack of a centralized Data Access Object (DAO) enforcing Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) parameterized calls.

docs.title: 5.1 Code Comparison (Before vs. After)
5.2 Defense-in-Depth Measures
docs.text:
1. Input Validation: Enforce strict type validation and whitelisting at the API boundary using schema validators (e.g. Joi, zod).
  2. Least Privilege: Ensure database connection accounts run with minimum required permissions (no administrative or DDL rights).
  3. WAF & Rate Limiting: Implement edge protections to mitigate brute-force attempts and anomalous payload signatures.

docs.title: 6.1 Retesting Procedure
docs.text:
1. Apply the recommended patch to the local codebase.
  2. Re-run the reproduction payload using Burp Suite Repeater.
  3. Verify that the server returns 400 Bad Request or safely escaped results without executing the payload.

docs.title: Finding the Hidden Score Board
docs.text: Field Details Challenge ID CH-T1-01 Difficulty Tier ★☆☆☆☆☆ (1-Star) Category Security Misconfiguration / Information Disclosure OWASP Top 10 (2021) A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration CWE ID CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor CVSS v3.1 Base Score 3.1 (Low) — CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N Target Technology Angular (SPA) / TypeScript Routing

docs.title: 1.1 Executive Overview
docs.text:
Modern Single Page Applications (SPAs) built with frameworks like Angular or React compile routing rules into client-side JavaScript bundles. In this application, developers intentionally hid the Score Board challenge tracker from standard navigation menus, assuming that omitting visible UI links would prevent unauthorized or public access.

This anti-pattern is known as Security through Obscurity. Because the entire routing table is delivered directly to the end-user's browser, unauthenticated visitors can reverse-engineer internal paths and access administrative or unlisted functionality directly.

docs.title: 1.2 Business Impact Analysis
docs.text:
• Confidentiality: Exposure of internal operational dashboards, system tracking metrics, or unreleased feature interfaces to untrusted parties.
  • Integrity: Potential reconnaissance leverage for attackers to discover high-value endpoints or debug interfaces.
  • Compliance & Governance: Failure to enforce strict role-based access control (RBAC) at both client and server boundaries violates principle-of-least-privilege guidelines (NIST SP 800-53, ISO 27001).

docs.title: 2.1 Inspection Workflow
docs.text:
1. Opened the target web application at http://localhost:3000 using Google Chrome Developer Tools (F12).
  2. Navigated to the Sources tab to analyze loaded client-side bundles under localhost:3000.
  3. Located the primary compiled application bundle (main.js).
  4. Reformatted the minified JavaScript using the Pretty-print ({}) utility to facilitate source inspection.
  5. Executed a targeted string query (Ctrl + F) searching for route declarations matching score-board and path:.
  6. Discovered the unauthenticated client-side route definition: 
    { path: "score-board", component: ScoreBoardComponent }

docs.title: 2.2 Attack Surface Sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Attacker as Security Tester
    participant Browser as Browser (DevTools)
    participant Client as Angular Client Router
    participant View as Score Board View

    Attacker->>Browser: Inspect main.js bundle
    Browser-->>Attacker: Disclose route definition 'score-board'
    Attacker->>Client: Navigate to http://target/#/score-board
    Client->>Client: Evaluate route table (No Guard present)
    Client-->>View: Render Score Board interface
    View-->>Attacker: Full access to challenge tracker

docs.title: 3. Proof of Concept (PoC) & Exploitation
docs.text: [!NOTE] Testing was performed in a local, isolated Docker container environment for defensive audit purposes.

docs.title: 3.1 Step-by-Step Reproduction
docs.text:
1. Launch the application in the web browser at http://localhost:3000.
  2. Inspect main.js in DevTools to confirm the route naming convention.

Figure 1: Client-side source code audit in Developer Tools revealing the unlisted score-board route.

  1. Manually append /#/score-board to the browser address bar: 
    GET /#/score-board HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
  2. The Angular client immediately resolves the route and instantiates the ScoreBoardComponent.
  3. The application confirms verification of the vulnerability with a success notification banner.

Figure 2: Accessing the Score Board interface and receiving the challenge resolution notification.

docs.title: 4.1 Vulnerable Source Code
docs.text:
• Repository File: frontend/src/app/app.routing.ts
  • Component: ScoreBoardComponent
// VULNERABLE ROUTE CONFIGURATION
const routes: Routes = [
  {
    path: 'score-board',
    component: ScoreBoardComponent
    // ⚠️ Flaw: No route guard (canActivate) is attached to enforce authentication or role verification
  },
  // ... other routes
]

docs.title: 4.2 Root Cause Breakdown
docs.text:
• Client-Side Absence of Guards: The Angular router configuration defines score-board as a public top-level route without implementing an Angular CanActivate guard interface.
  • Architectural Misconception: Reliance on UI menu omission rather than cryptographic or state-based access verification to restrict sensitive views.

docs.title: 5.1 Code Comparison (Before vs. After)
5.2 Defense-in-Depth Measures
docs.text:
1. Server-Side API Authorization: Frontend route guards provide user experience protection, but the backend API endpoint serving scorecard data (/api/Challenges) must independently validate the user's JWT token and permissions on every request.
  2. Bundle Hardening: In production applications, administrative routes and components should be encapsulated in lazily-loaded feature modules (loadChildren) accessible only after successful authentication, reducing the footprint of the public main.js bundle.

docs.title: 6.1 Retesting Procedure
docs.text:
1. Apply the canActivate: [AuthGuard] guard to the route configuration.
  2. Attempt direct navigation to http://localhost:3000/#/score-board in an unauthenticated browser session.
  3. Confirm that the application redirects the user to /#/login with an access-denied flash message.

docs.text:
• OWASP Top 10:2021: A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration
  • CWE Definition: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
  • Angular Documentation: Controlling Access with Route Guards
  • OWASP Cheat Sheet: Authorization Cheat Sheet

docs.title: 2.1 Target Application (OWASP Juice Shop)
docs.text:
• Container Image: bkimminich/juice-shop:latest
  • Application Stack:
  • Frontend: Angular Single Page Application (SPA), Angular Material
  • Backend API: Node.js, Express.js

docs.text:
• Interception Proxy: Burp Suite (Community / Professional)

  • Active extensions: Logger++, Auto-Repeater, JSON Web Tokens (JWT) Editor.
  • Client Analysis: Chromium & Firefox Developer Tools (Network Inspector, Console, Storage, Sources).
  • Automation & Scripting: Python 3 (requests, beautifulsoup4), curl, sqlmap (for verification).
  • Source Code Reference: Upstream GitHub repository clone used for side-by-side white-box line auditing.

docs.title: 3. Laboratory Hygiene & State Management
docs.text:
• Backup & Reset: The lab can be restored to a clean state at any moment by restarting the Docker container: 
    docker stop juice-shop && docker run -d --rm -p 3000:3000 --name juice-shop bkimminich/juice-shop
  • Evidence Archival: All raw HTTP requests, responses, and screenshots are organized per challenge in the assets/images/tier-X/ directory for reproducible audits.

docs.title: Application Security Testing Framework
docs.text: This document outlines the testing methodology, scoring rubric, and ethical rules of engagement followed throughout the OWASP Juice Shop security assessment.

docs.title: 1. Industry Standard Alignment
docs.text:
The assessment strictly aligns with the OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG v4.2) framework, which structures web application security testing across 12 distinct categories:

WSTG ID Category Description Application in Juice Shop Audit WSTG-INFO Information Gathering & Reconnaissance Endpoint discovery, robots.txt, client-side source map audits WSTG-CONF Configuration & Deployment Management Server banners, error stack traces, CORS misconfigurations WSTG-IDNT Identity Management Testing User enumeration, account registration flaws WSTG-ATHN Authentication Testing SQL injection bypass, password reset weakness, brute-force WSTG-ATHZ Authorization Testing Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR), privilege escalation WSTG-SESS Session Management Testing JWT tampering, session fixation, token expiration analysis WSTG-INPV Input Validation Testing XSS (DOM/Reflected), SQLi, NoSQLi, XXE, Command Injection WSTG-ERRH Error Handling Leaked internal exceptions, database error disclosure WSTG-CRYP Cryptography Weak ciphers, insecure hash algorithms (MD5/SHA1) WSTG-BUSL Business Logic Testing Basket manipulation, checkout workflow bypasses WSTG-CLNT Client-Side Testing DOM-based injection, HTML5 storage abuse, WebSockets WSTG-APIT API Testing Mass assignment, unauthorized parameter inspection

docs.title: 2. Vulnerability Scoring (CVSS v3.1)
docs.text:
Every vulnerability identified in this portfolio is scored according to the CVSS v3.1 (Common Vulnerability Scoring System) standard to establish objective severity:

pie title CVSS v3.1 Severity Distribution Target
    "Critical (9.0 - 10.0)" : 15
    "High (7.0 - 8.9)" : 35
    "Medium (4.0 - 6.9)" : 38

docs.title: Metrics Evaluated:
docs.text:
• Attack Vector (AV): Network (AV:N) / Local (AV:L)
  • Attack Complexity (AC): Low (AC:L) / High (AC:H)
  • Privileges Required (PR): None (PR:N) / Low (PR:L) / High (PR:H)
  • User Interaction (UI): None (UI:N) / Required (UI:R)
  • Scope (S): Unchanged (S:U) / Changed (S:C)
  • Impact (CIA): Confidentiality (C), Integrity (I), Availability (A)

docs.title: 3. White-Box Code Review Methodology
docs.text:
Unlike pure black-box penetration testing, this portfolio incorporates White-Box Application Security Reviews:

  1. Static Analysis & Inspection:
  2. Reviewing Angular frontend client bundles and component templates.
  3. Inspecting Node.js / Express routes, middleware, and Sequelize ORM models.
  4. Root Cause Identification:
  5. Tracing untrusted inputs from the req object down to database queries or template rendering.
  6. Patch Engineering:
  7. Formulating functional, production-ready code fixes adhering to the principle of least privilege and defense-in-depth.

    Tier 6 (6★ Expert Chains)       :2026-11-14, 5d

docs.title: OWASP Top 10:2021 Vulnerability Mapping
docs.text: This taxonomy matrix indexes all challenges in OWASP Juice Shop by their corresponding OWASP Top 10:2021 standard category.

docs.title: A01:2021 - Broken Access Control
docs.text:
• Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR): Accessing other users' shopping baskets.
  • Vertical & Horizontal Privilege Escalation.
  • Confidential Document Exposure (/ftp directory traversal).
  • Unvalidated Redirects & Forwards.

docs.title: A02:2021 - Cryptographic Failures
docs.text:
• Weak password hashing algorithms (MD5).
  • Exposed private keys & unprotected JWT secrets.
  • Insecure direct file downloads of cryptographic keys.

docs.title: A03:2021 - Injection
docs.text:
• SQL Injection: Authentication bypass, union-based schema leakage.
  • Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): DOM-based, Reflected, and Stored XSS vectors.
  • NoSQL Injection: MongoDB parameter manipulation.
  • Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) & Command Injection.

docs.title: A04:2021 - Insecure Design
docs.text:
• Bypassing client-side star rating limits (Zero Stars Feedback).
  • Repetitive password registration validation bypass.
  • Business logic bypass in promo codes and wallet checkout.

docs.title: A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration
docs.text:
• Default administrative credentials.
  • Verbose stack traces and debug error message disclosure.
  • Unprotected cloud storage buckets and API endpoints.

docs.title: A06:2021 - Vulnerable and Outdated Components
docs.text:
• Known CVE exploitation in outdated npm dependencies.
  • XML External Entity (XXE) in legacy XML parsing libraries.

docs.title: A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures
docs.text:
• Weak password reset security questions.
  • Missing rate limiting on login endpoints (Brute-force risk).
  • Insecure multi-factor authentication (MFA) implementation.

docs.title: A08:2021 - Software and Data Integrity Failures
docs.text:
• Insecure deserialization in user-controlled serialized state.
  • Unsigned or self-signed JWT token acceptance (alg: none).

docs.title: A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
docs.text:
• Failure to log unauthorized access attempts.
  • Inadequate audit trails on financial and administrative transactions.

docs.title: A10:2021 - Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
docs.text:
• Bypassing internal whitelist checks to query loopback interfaces.
  • Interacting with cloud instance metadata services via profile image uploads.

docs.title: Secure Coding Guidelines: Node.js, Express & Angular
docs.text: This guide consolidates defensive engineering principles and remediation patterns identified across the OWASP Juice Shop application security assessment.

docs.title: 1.1 SQL & NoSQL Injection Defense
docs.text:
• Sequelize ORM Parameterization: Never concatenate untrusted strings into raw SQL queries. 
    // ❌ VULNERABLE
sequelize.query(`SELECT * FROM Products WHERE id = ${req.params.id}`);

// ✅ SECURE
sequelize.query('SELECT * FROM Products WHERE id = :id', {
  replacements: { id: req.params.id },
  type: QueryTypes.SELECT
});
  • NoSQL Query Sanitization: Use mongo-sanitize to strip $ and . operators from request bodies to prevent operator injection ({"$gt": ""}).

docs.title: 1.2 Access Control & Authorization (IDOR Defense)
docs.text:
• Always validate that the authenticated user (req.user.id) owns the requested object before fetching or mutating records. 
    // ❌ VULNERABLE (IDOR)
const basket = await BasketModel.findByPk(req.params.basketId);

// ✅ SECURE
const basket = await BasketModel.findOne({
  where: {
    id: req.params.basketId,
    UserId: req.user.id
  }
});
if (!basket) return res.status(404).json({ error: "Basket not found" });

docs.title: 1.3 Security Headers & Middleware
docs.text:
• Integrate Helmet.js to automatically set modern HTTP defense headers: 
    const helmet = require('helmet');
app.use(helmet({
  contentSecurityPolicy: {
    directives: {
      defaultSrc: ["'self'"],
      scriptSrc: ["'self'"],
      objectSrc: ["'none'"]
    }
  },
  frameguard: { action: 'deny' },
  hsts: { maxAge: 31536000, includeSubDomains: true }
}));

docs.title: 2.1 Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Prevention
docs.text:
• Rely on Angular's built-in contextual encoding:
  • Use {{ expression }} or [property]="value" bindings.
  • Avoid DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml() unless strictly validated and sanitized with DOMPurify.
  • Never use native ElementRef.nativeElement.innerHTML = ....

docs.title: 2.2 Client-Side Route Guards & Authentication
docs.text: • Frontend route guards (canActivate) are for user experience only. All business logic and data access must be authoritatively enforced on the backend API server.
